governing_spec.section: Section B: Journal Consumer Isolation & Old-Writer Retirement

transactional_cas_writes.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: Atomic multi-store transaction with bundle file locking and crash recovery bound strictly to durable transaction identity (_tx_id, scoped idempotency_key, tenant, actor, user, request, and entry). Reservation is registered in idempotency store with status pending. Domain creation transactions use domain_creation_idempotency_key ('domain:create:{quoted_tenant}:{quoted_actor}:{quoted_entry}'), fully separated from BFF request identity ('create:{quoted_tenant}:{quoted_user}:{quoted_key}'). Recovery coordinates secondary writes outside locks, then acquires bundle_lock() and _tx_lock, re-reads fresh entry, verifies _creation_outbox is still present, and commits via compare_and_set, preserving any concurrent committed patches without clobbering. Read and replay fail closed while creation remains incomplete. DecisionJournalOwnerAdapter._recover_committed_entry_result and check/await_create_idempotency strictly bind replay to actual committed creation transactions with successful secondary writes and exact tenant/user scope matches, never promoting live provisional rows to succeeded or leaking cross-scope results.

append_only_audit_with_diff.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: patch_entry computes changedFields, diff changes (before/after) and appends audit record bound to actor_id, user_id, tenant_id, and transaction idempotency key. list_audit_events strictly enforces tenant scope, authorized principal on audit reads, and gates event visibility on committed transaction outcome, never disclosing uncommitted or rolled-back provisional events to preserve append-only externally visible history.

durable_outbox_streaming.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: outbox record store initialized and populated on entry creation and updates with decision_journal.entry.* event types with explicit tenant_id, actor_id, user_id, and idempotency key scoping. Creation includes its idempotency and outbox under bundle_lock; list_outbox_events gates visibility on committed transaction outcome so readers cannot observe or publish provisional/aborted creates or updates, and fresh-process retries after creation crash recover and emit the creation outbox event. Replay/recreate of committed entries preserves original event payload and never emits duplicate creation events.

tenant_and_user_isolation.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: Unified fail-closed _get_committed_entry_snapshot resolution and _is_entry_accessible policy across get_entry, list_entries, DecisionJournalOwnerAdapter detail/list, DomainDecisionJournalReaderPort detail/list, and InMemoryOperationsConsultationPort. Tenant-scoped records strictly require matching tenant; tenant-only queries without actor deny private records; unscoped queries deny tenant-scoped records; legacy records missing tenant require explicit include_unscoped_legacy=True (ordinary unscoped reads denied even for authored legacy); and private records require matching authorized principal (actor_id/user_id). list_entries consistently preserves the before_entry snapshot during incomplete or uncommitted patches across crashed recoveries, preventing private metadata or body disclosure across principals. Delimiters in tenants/users/keys are URL-quoted with safe='-_.~' across all idempotency keys to prevent delimiter collision. Recovery and replay strictly validate tenant_id, user_id, and entry_id against stored reservations and result payloads so crashed or forged reservations never replay other principals' records across ambiguous scope boundaries.

caller_supplied_id_collision_rejection.implementation: services/governance/decision_journal.py: create_entry raises DecisionJournalCollisionError when a supplied ID collides with another principal's or tenant's record. Domain creation transaction keys ('domain:create:...') are fully isolated from BFF request idempotency keys ('create:...'), preventing supplied IDs from aliasing or overwriting request-level reservations. Recreate of an already-committed entry by same owner never deletes the pre-existing row on outbox failure and retains canonical identity. AgoraService and DecisionJournalOwnerAdapter bind create reservation and result durably to recoverable durable transaction; crashed creator reservations are safely reclaimed or recovered on retry without 409 idempotency conflict.

controlled_legacy_migration.implementation: services/governance/migrations/journal_migration.py: JournalMigrationEngine verifies principal ownership (createdBy/actor_id/userId) and SHA-256 checksum parity before destination mutation or disposition. Unscoped destination collisions with mismatched author or content are strictly rejected as conflicts. Requires or recovers checksum/principal/action-bound durable migration audit (governance.decision_journal.migrated or legacy_scoped) before every disposal path, including skipped_identical and checkpoint resume; source is strictly preserved on missing proof or general patch audit.

unscoped_legacy_isolation.implementation: Ordinary unscoped reads (include_unscoped_legacy=False) fail closed on legacy rows missing tenant_id even if authored by caller; governed legacy access (include_unscoped_legacy=True) required. Ordinary patch strictly requires clean_tenant and fails closed on unscoped legacy rows pending governed migration; missing scope matrix verified across all readers and adapters.

fresh_process_restart_parity.implementation: CoordinatingJsonGovernanceRecordStore uses POSIX file locking (fcntl.flock) and cache invalidation on get/list_all/put/insert_if_absent/compare_and_set/delete to guarantee that multiple long-lived store instances across processes and threads coordinate safely without cache clobbering or losing committed records.
